entities.name: Gorgippus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gorgippus was a son of Satyrus I and a key figure in the Bosporan Kingdom's struggle for power.

As a Spartocid joint ruler with his brother Leucon, Gorgippus sought to solidify his position on the Asiatic side of the kingdom, establishing his seat of power in Gorgippia.

His reign was marked by a series of diplomatic and military maneuvers aimed at expanding the kingdom's influence in the region.

Gorgippus's legacy can be seen in the continued presence of the Bosporan Kingdom as a major player in the ancient world, albeit in a reduced capacity compared to its peak during the 4th century BCE.

"The future of the Bosporans is tied to the fortunes of the Greeks," Gorgippus is quoted as saying in a 349 BCE letter to his brother, highlighting the complex web of alliances and rivalries that defined the ancient world.
